newsitem.title: UK: European refinery output fell in May - Euroil.
newsitem.headline: European refinery output fell in May - Euroil.

text.p: Refinery output in Europe fell 0.5 percent to 12.257 million barrels per day (bpd) in May compared to April, Stichting Euroilstock said in its latest monthly report.
Crude intake was down 1.6 percent to 11.704 million bpd in May which represents a utilisation rate of 88.67 percent, the report said. In April utilisation was 90.13 percent.
Stichting Euroilstock reports data for the 15 countries of the European Union plus Norway.
Gasoline output or production rose 1.2 percent in April to 3.34 million bpd but was 0.9 percent below year ago levels.
Middle distillate production was up 0.9 percent at 5.67 million bpd in April and was some 6.4 percent above year ago levels.

Fuel oil production fell 1.5 percent to 1.813 million in April but this was still some 11.1 percent above May 1996. Naphtha production fell 1.8 percent to 951,000 bpd in May but was 8.9 percent above year ago levels.
Figures are based on refinery capacity of 12.6 million bpd. Refinery intake represents crude oil only and excludes natural gas liquids, feedstocks and other inputs.
